evidence.exact_quote: - UI returns idle with preserved history

items.impact: A user interrupt has an explicit visible terminal condition that preserves history rather than erasing the interrupted session.
items.statement: GRS-034 explicitly requires the UI to return to idle while preserving history after interruption.
items.title: Interrupt settles to visible idle with history

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: 'Define cancellation propagation and settlement: provider stream, subprocess, MCP call, browser/device, child run; no conversion to success/failure; history interruption boundary.'
- Stop active MCP call leaves partial/cancelled result

items.impact: Implementations can diverge on subprocess, browser/device, and child-run cancellation, especially when completion races cancellation or a transport is offline, and still satisfy the listed MCP/provider/UI checks.
items.statement: GRS-034 names five propagation surfaces, but its acceptance oracles directly cover only an MCP call, a provider stream, and UI history; it does not define cancellation-vs-completion precedence, timeout settlement, idempotent repeated stop, or receipts for the other surfaces.
items.title: Cancellation propagation is broader than its oracles

evidence.exact_quote: - A child/subagent cannot exceed parent ceiling even if model/tool output requests it.

items.impact: The parent envelope is an explicit hard ceiling, preventing child output from self-escalating runtime authority.
items.statement: GRS-035 makes the parent control ceiling authoritative over child model or tool requests.
items.title: Parent envelope is a hard authority ceiling

evidence.exact_quote: proposal_or_recommendation: Define AgentControlEnvelope with autonomy_mode, write_surface, provider/model/effort policy, tool/MCP permission ceiling, context/token budgets, loop budgets, wall-clock budgets, terminal/browser/device authority, child-spawn policy, cancellation/steering semantics, progress heartbeat, and receipt refs.

items.impact: Different runtimes can serialize, inherit, mutate, expire, and enforce the same-named envelope differently; mid-run steering and concurrent updates can produce mismatched effective authority or budget accounting.
items.statement: GRS-035 enumerates envelope fields but does not define field types, required/default values, inheritance/merge precedence, revision and effective-at boundaries, violation outcomes, sensitive-field retention, or aggregate budget accounting under concurrency.
items.title: AgentControlEnvelope lacks deterministic lifecycle semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Parent cannot certify complete until all required child results are settled or explicitly waived.

items.impact: Parent completion is prevented from silently ignoring required child results.
items.statement: GRS-036 explicitly gates parent certification on settlement or waiver of every required child result.
items.title: Child settlement gates parent certification

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: 'PM needs a single child execution lifecycle independent of prompt packets: spawn, admitted context, first event, heartbeat, partial result, await, cancellation, orphan reap, result settlement, and parent completion gating.'

items.impact: Cancellation, late results, timeouts, parent crashes, waivers, and orphan cleanup can race without a shared winner rule, leaving child authority and parent completion nondeterministic.
items.statement: GRS-036 lists lifecycle stages but does not define legal transitions, terminal-state precedence, late-result handling, waiver authority and evidence, crash/restart recovery, or orphan-reaper idempotency.
items.title: Subagent lifecycle has no race-safe state machine

evidence.exact_quote: - Fixtures for each loop family stop within bounded attempts.

items.impact: Each loop family has an explicit falsifiable expectation that it terminates within a bound.
items.statement: GRS-037 requires a bounded-stop fixture for every registered loop family.
items.title: Loop families require bounded-stop fixtures

evidence.exact_quote: proposal_or_recommendation: 'Add LoopBreakerRegistry with typed families: identical_tool_failure, empty_assistant, no_tool_progress, repeated_edit_miss, compaction_no_gain, context_overflow_replay, MCP_resource_missing, first_event_timeout, transport_idle, reasoning_no_action, subagent_same_read, and spend_anomaly. Each family has fingerprint, max_count, required observation window, terminal action, and user-facing reason.'

items.impact: Builders must invent fingerprints, thresholds, windows, and terminal actions, so the same run may stop in one runtime and continue in another; false positives have no defined safe resume or override path.
items.statement: GRS-037 names the required parameters for each loop family but supplies no values or derivation rules, fingerprint versioning, cross-family precedence, distributed/parallel aggregation semantics, or recovery from a mistaken stop.
items.title: Loop breaker taxonomy leaves enforcement discretionary

evidence.exact_quote: - Every subagent receives a ChildAgentLease with parent_goal_id, allowed_phase, read/write mode, max_depth, cannot_resume_parent_goal=true, and terminal return channel.

items.impact: A child receives an explicit scope and cannot legitimately assume the parent goal identity.
items.statement: GRS-038 defines a ChildAgentLease carrying parent identity, allowed phase, access mode, depth, a parent-resume prohibition, and return channel.
items.title: ChildAgentLease bounds goal identity

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: AgentControlEnvelope covered authority, but not enough about inheritable goal identity, child-agent leases, or proving that a child cannot resume/advance the parent goal.

items.impact: A stale or duplicated child may retain usable authority after cancellation, parent restart, replan, or reconnect because lease freshness and revocation cannot be proven consistently.
items.statement: GRS-038 lists lease contents and restrictions but does not define issuer identity, signing or binding, lease revision/expiry, renewal, revocation propagation, replay prevention, or crash/restart reconciliation.
items.title: Child leases lack lifecycle and anti-replay rules

evidence.exact_quote: - External agent output/tool requests enter PM as untrusted until settled by PM receipts.

items.impact: Imported output cannot immediately exercise native PM authority merely because it came from a supported external agent.
items.statement: GRS-039 explicitly classifies external output and tool requests as untrusted until PM receipt settlement.
items.title: External agent output starts untrusted

evidence.exact_quote: - Imported external-agent session has source tool/version, authority surface, context lineage, credential handling, cwd/worktree, terminal/session transcript, and continuation mode.

items.impact: Malformed or hostile handoff data can be interpreted inconsistently, while credentials and transcripts may be retained or displayed without a deterministic redaction, encryption, expiry, and deletion policy.
items.statement: GRS-039 names provenance fields and credential handling but does not define import parsing limits, schema/version compatibility, sanitization, secret redaction and retention, receipt trust-promotion criteria, partial-import rollback, or conflict resolution when local and external histories diverge.
items.title: External handoff validation and data lifecycle are open

evidence.exact_quote: External agent sessions, MCP config imports, and handoff packets enter PM as untrusted provenance/evidence until settled by PM receipts. Imported sessions do not become native PM authority or bypass Goal, Tool, or Permission ownership.

items.impact: The constraint preserves Goal, Tool, and Permission ownership against authority laundering through imported sessions or configuration.
items.statement: GRS-040 explicitly prevents imported sessions from becoming native authority or bypassing existing ownership boundaries.
items.title: Imported sessions cannot bypass native ownership

evidence.exact_quote: - atom-0121 source details remain traceable through source_lineage and preserved source fields.

items.impact: Traceability can pass while an importer still grants native authority or bypasses Goal, Tool, or Permission checks; the central safety claim is therefore not directly falsified by the acceptance surface.
items.statement: GRS-040's only behavior-specific acceptance criterion proves source traceability, not rejection, quarantine, receipt settlement, or non-bypass across the three named owners.
items.title: Import guardrail lacks a non-bypass test

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not re-own Executor scheduling, storage replay, permission enforcement, or provider/model/account resolution.

items.impact: Goal Runtime's event closure is prevented from silently absorbing scheduling, replay, permission, or identity authority from their canonical owners.
items.statement: GRS-041 explicitly constrains its ownership to Goal Runtime semantics while consuming other owners' contracts.
items.title: Event closure preserves cross-document ownership

evidence.exact_quote: - The common payload envelope includes event_name, schema_version, occurred_at_utc, project/thread/goal identity, revisions, actor/execution role, requested/effective provider/model/account refs, correlation/causation/idempotency, evidence/artifact refs, approval refs, and block refs.
- All 15 goal events and all 6 goal_run events list event-specific payload minima.

items.impact: Consumers can disagree on required fields, unknown-event behavior, revision compatibility, replay after partial writes, and owner-contract mismatch while aggregate count checks still pass.
items.statement: GRS-041 requires a shared envelope and per-event minima but does not state schema-version compatibility and migration rules, required-vs-optional field matrices, unknown-field/event handling, replay/rollback behavior for partial persistence, or deterministic reconciliation when consumed owner contracts change.
items.title: Event closure lacks evolution and per-event falsifiability rules

segments.summary: GRS-034 through GRS-037 establish cancellation settlement, an agent-control ceiling, child-result gating, and typed loop breakers. The intent is strong, but deterministic state transitions, race precedence, schema/lifecycle rules, concrete enforcement parameters, recovery paths, and surface-complete acceptance oracles remain materially underspecified.

GRS-038 through GRS-041 establish child goal leases, untrusted external-session handoff, a non-bypass import guardrail, and Goal Runtime event-envelope ownership. Major gaps remain in lease revocation/replay safety, hostile and sensitive import handling, executable non-bypass tests, and versioned per-event schema/recovery semantics across owner seams.
